title: A 200 K BT-Settl surface contrast fits eight optical dip depths of TIC 262400835 with dust opacity index 2
abstract: We test whether the optical colors of two CPV dips require a dust opacity index above 2. We integrate MuSCAT2 responses against BT-Settl spectra and test every nonnegative dust column. A fixed linear bound holds for opacity indices 0 to 2 in 36 single-spectrum and response models. The 15 December 2020 depths of TIC 262400835 violate it by 3.734 stated errors under independent Gaussian errors, or 2.303 with the largest covariance allowed by the marginal errors. Band integration thus keeps the earlier conditional discrepancy. A surface with 2/3 projected area at 3000 K and 1/3 at 3200 K changes the result. Dust with opacity index 2 covering only cool light fits all eight ground-based depths from 13 and 15 December with chi-square 4.8875 and five fitted screen values. Every residual is below 1.60 stated errors. Both nights use the same surface mixture. A finite-column construction reaches 1.370 errors. A log(g)=4.0 check stays below 1.89 errors, but raises the first-night covered area from 12% to 67% of the disk. Planck spectra with the same temperatures do worse. This is a data-based color degeneracy and a bandpass test, not a measured surface map or dust composition. Unknown depth covariance, synthetic spectra, digitized responses, selective cool-region coverage and omitted cloud geometry limit the result. Original code, input hashes, aggregate evidence and separate-scratch repeat steps are included. External spectra and response tables are excluded.

display.caption: Left: the single-spectrum certificate with independent errors and the largest error allowed by unknown covariance. The dashed threshold uses the earlier 24-test family. Middle: largest residuals of the fixed two-temperature surface fit. Right: constructed light-loss spectra of the fitted dust screens over the cool component. No external spectrum or response curve is shown.
